cross_insight: The AI revolution is rapidly moving from model training to large-scale inference, causing a massive shortage of high-capacity HBM and shifting the hardware bottleneck from raw compute to power grids, advanced packaging, and network bandwidth. Tech companies are actively building out infrastructure, with Cisco expanding into cloud control via the Splunk acquisition and LG Innotek achieving a 93% yield on FC-BGA substrate lines while planning next-gen glass substrates. To address the severe electricity bottleneck, tech giants are increasingly focusing on power-efficient designs, such as on-chip S-RAM, optical communications (CPO), and securing long-term nuclear energy sources.
divergence: A key debate centers on whether the current AI buildout is approaching a short-term bubble burst due to white-collar job displacement and rising electricity costs, or if the massive capital allocation by cloud hyperscalers will continue uninterrupted, supported by a transition from 'token maxing' (brute-force computing) to 'outcome maxing' (efficient, specialized agents).
key_themes: AI inference bottleneck shifting to power grids, FC-BGA, and MLCCs
Transition to outcome-focused, cost-efficient AI routing and 'Vibe Coding'
Advanced packaging innovation (glass substrates, CPO, and OSAT partnerships)
watch_list: Samsung Electro-Mechanics & LG Innotek (advanced substrates and MLCC)
Google (TPU ecosystem and Google Flow adoption)
